title: Fixed particle attenuation limits the measured export contribution to ALOHA oxygen stock loss to 0.30 mol/m2
abstract: We test whether measured passive carbon export can support the 300-700 m oxygen stock loss at Station ALOHA. We use HOT trap data through 2024 and a published oxygen stock series. In a renewal box with zero added deficit at the start of 1997, fixed power-law particle attenuation, and oxygen-to-carbon use of 138/106, the measured annual export history gives at most 0.30 mol O2/m2 of the 4.82 mol/m2 loss between 1989-1996 and 2009-2024. This is 6.2% of the total loss and 8.9% of the residual after density displacement. We prove a sharp bound of 0.286 on the fraction of 150 m flux lost between 300 and 700 m for any positive fixed power-law exponent. The measured cumulative anomaly is nonnegative, so no renewal bounds every constant renewal time from above. Baseline, treatment and season checks give point limits of 0.14-0.91 mol/m2. A sampling bootstrap gives a 0-1.24 mol/m2 range on the tested renewal grid. The minimum missing local carbon respiration step is 5.71 mg C/m2/day for the total loss, or 3.82 for the fixed-density residual. The result limits increased passive export with fixed attenuation. Changed particle breakdown depth, unmeasured carbon pathways, transport and upstream respiration remain possible. One station and sparse trap deployments limit inference.

display.caption: Measured passive export, oxygen stock deficit, and missing carbon respiration under fixed attenuation. All values are local and conditional on the stated renewal-box assumptions.
